name: Permanent Magnets Ltd
tagline: Sits inside India's rare-earth-magnet self-sufficiency push (REPM scheme, China curbs, subsidiary ECMS approval) but Q1 FY27 confirmed the operating weakness rather than an inflection: revenue +19% YoY yet PAT -14%, margins compressed to ~18.5%, Relays and Quantum Phase-2 timelines slipped, NdFeB magnet revenue still zero
business_overview: Permanent Magnets makes magnetic assemblies, current-sensing shunts, alloys, and Neodymium (NdFeB) magnet components for automotive/EV, smart electricity meters, and (increasingly) defense/aerospace applications, and is positioning for India's push to build a domestic rare-earth-magnet supply chain via subsidiary Quantum Magnetics.
fundamentals_table: ~57.7 (on ~Rs 15 Cr FY26 PAT, which itself fell from Rs 20 Cr FY24 / Rs 16 Cr FY25)
FY26 Rs 226 Cr (+10% YoY); Q1 FY27 standalone Rs 63.2 Cr (+19% YoY, Alloys-led)
~Rs 88 Cr (rising to fund Quantum/Relays/Alloys capex; equity dilution flagged as part of funding mix)
fundamentals_narrative: A trusted user's own Feb-2026 note was blunt: flat YoY revenue, compressed margins, tariff-hit exports — a genuinely weak period, not a hidden inflection. The Q1 FY27 print (Aug 2026) did not reverse that: standalone revenue rose 19% YoY to Rs 63.2 Cr on new Alloys capacity, but EBITDA margin fell to ~18.5% (from ~21%) and standalone PAT dropped 14% YoY to Rs 6.25 Cr (consolidated PAT Rs 3.80 Cr on higher interest). Three straight years of declining PAT (Rs 20 Cr FY24 -> Rs 16 Cr FY25 -> Rs 15 Cr FY26), ROCE drifting from 15% to ~14%, and rising debt to fund a Rs 80-100 Cr capex programme (Rs 40-50 Cr PML + Rs 40-50 Cr Quantum). The bull case rests entirely on forward optionality — India's REPM scheme, China export curbs, and Quantum Magnetics' Aug-2026 ECMS approval for Neodymium magnet manufacturing — none of which is yet in the P&L (rare-earth/magnet line had zero revenue in FY26). At ~57x trailing the optionality is heavily priced.
technical_read: Stock rallied ~30% in a week in mid-2025 on China rare-earth export-curb news, then gave up much of that gain as fundamentals stayed weak through early 2026; not independently charted this pass.
sentiment_summary: Read the most recent 50 of 82 fetched posts (2023-05 to 2026-08), single batch, from a long-running (97-post) thread. Early 2023 sentiment centered on the EV/smart-meter growth story and an auditor-integrity due-diligence flag (later judged historical/unrelated). By late 2023-2024, growth stalled (PAT fell ~50% YoY in one quarter) as the EV-magnet business slowed. From late 2025, sentiment pivoted almost entirely to the REPM (rare-earth permanent magnet) government scheme and China's export-curb-driven price spike, with the company's own operational performance becoming secondary to the macro thematic. The most recent post (2026-08-26) reports the related private company Quantum Magnetics receiving government approval under the Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) for Neodymium magnet manufacturing — relevant context, and (per Aug-2026 filings) Quantum is a PML subsidiary, so this one is company-specific.
community_signal: Trusted user T11 wrote an early, well-received (28 loves) deep-dive on the NdFeB magnet landscape's strategic importance in 2023. Trusted user karanshah137 explained the REPM scheme's 'mine-to-magnet' value-chain logic in detail (Nov-Dec 2025). Trusted user siddybee (15 loves) gave the most recent and most balanced take (Feb 2026): despite a ~40% stock decline and weak recent fundamentals (flat revenue, margin compression, tariff-hit exports), the company may be 'sitting on a BIG opportunity' in rare earth magnets — an explicitly forward-looking, unconfirmed thesis.

trusted_signals.note: Detailed writeup on NdFeB magnets' criticality in defense and EV/wind applications and expected >3x demand growth over 7 years, framing the long-term strategic case (well before the 2025-26 REPM catalyst crystallized).

Acknowledged the stock is down ~40% from his prior writeup with flat revenue, compressed margins, and tariff-hit exports, but argued the company may be 'sitting on a BIG opportunity' given rare-earth-magnet criticality — explicitly framed as a forward, unconfirmed thesis, not a current-fundamentals call.

Explained India's REPM scheme is targeting integrated magnet manufacturing (alloying through magnet-making), the value-added end of the chain most relevant to a company like Permanent Magnets, though did not confirm the company's specific participation.

bse_notes: A 2023 due-diligence post flagged the company's then-auditor had been SEBI-fined in an unrelated ~2010-11 matter (a different client, IPO-proceeds siphoning) — historical, not connected to Permanent Magnets' own governance, and not an active action against the company. Aug 2026: subsidiary Quantum Magnetics Pvt Ltd received ECMS approval to manufacture Neodymium magnets.
bull_case: Structural, government-backed tailwind (REPM 'mine-to-magnet' scheme, Rs 7,280 Cr) directly targets the rare-earth-magnet value chain this company already operates in; PML has submitted a bid
Company-specific proof point now on the board: subsidiary Quantum Magnetics received ECMS approval (Aug 2026) for Neodymium magnet manufacturing — no longer purely thematic
China's rare-earth export curbs (2025-26) are driving real price/demand dynamics in India's favor, independent of company-specific execution
Long-standing defense/aerospace credibility (ISRO Chandrayaan components, current-sensing shunts for smart meters) gives a base business to fund the optionality
Alloys division new capacity is commissioned and driving the +19% Q1 FY27 top line
bear_case: Q1 FY27 confirmed weakness rather than an inflection: revenue +19% YoY but EBITDA margin down to ~18.5% and PAT -14% YoY; three straight years of falling PAT (Rs 20 -> 16 -> 15 Cr)
No confirmed REPM-scheme allocation — bids from 20 applicants opened Aug 2026, only 5 will be selected; the flagship catalyst is still binary and unowned
Rare-earth/NdFeB magnet revenue was zero in FY26; the Rs 80-100 Cr capex to build it is funded partly by debt (now ~Rs 88 Cr) and explicitly-flagged equity dilution
Relays (high-margin) commercial ramp slipped to H2 FY27; Quantum Phase-2 slipped to Q3 FY27 — execution timelines have repeatedly moved right
~57x trailing P/E already prices heavy optionality onto a company earning ~Rs 15 Cr and with declining ROCE (~14%) / ROE (10.5%)
Magnet-less EV motor technology (e.g., Sona Comstar) is a nascent but real long-term substitution risk to the automotive magnet business
verdict_headline: A government-scale structural catalyst (rare-earth self-sufficiency) sitting on top of a company whose Q1 FY27 print confirmed weak execution — PAT still falling, margins compressed, key projects delayed, no REPM allocation won, rare-earth revenue still zero
verdict_reasoning: Pre-pass this was held at 10x-in-2-3-years / Low under the small-cap inflection rule, pending a confirming recent quarter. The Q1 FY27 quarter (Aug 2026) went the other way: +19% revenue but -14% PAT, margin compression, and slipped Relays/Quantum timelines. Weak trailing average + weak confirming quarter + still-thematic catalyst -> thesis_fit drops to 'neither'.

four_box score 2.0 (tailwind yes; tam weak — zero rare-earth revenue and no confirmed allocation; moat weak; valuation no at ~57x on declining earnings). No written exception applies (valuation box is 'no', growth is not un-ignorable given PAT is falling), so 'neither' is the hard call.

Conviction stays Low. What would move it: PML winning a REPM allocation (bid results due within ~3-6 months), Quantum Phase-2 commissioning on the revised Q3 FY27 schedule, or a genuine margin/PAT inflection. The Quantum ECMS approval is a real incremental positive but is a small scheme win, not revenue.

A trusted user (siddybee) made almost exactly the 'weak fundamentals, real but unconfirmed optionality' argument directly — which keeps this on the watch list rather than screened out, but does not support a return-magnitude label yet.
